label: 4 PM refresh
note: 155 verified quotes from 92 voices. 15 of 17 members of Congress on record oppose or question the move, now including Jeffries, Cramer, Curtis and Ricketts; none support it. Oppenheimer, StoneX and Melius upgraded. Yale's Sonnenfeld: "we have seen no weaker board." NVDA +30.9% at 1:42 PM ET; the official close was not yet published and will be added at 7 PM.

label: 7 PM refresh
note: Official close added: NVDA closed at $165.05, up 31.5%, adding about $950 billion; peers and indexes now show closing moves. 180 verified quotes from 105 voices, including The Atlantic's Tom Nichols and Fox Business's Charles Gasparino. Still no foreign government reaction.

label: 9 PM refresh
note: 222 verified quotes from 133 voices. 27 of the 29 members of Congress on record oppose or question the reinstatement, now including Van Hollen, Schiff, Wyden and Republican Tom Cotton; Gov. Josh Shapiro and far-right commentator Laura Loomer joined the critics. Israel's Netanyahu is the first world leader on record, and he welcomed it. In Asia on Tuesday, TSMC and Hon Hai opened limit-up. No after-hours NVDA quote was published.

label: Nov 24 recap
note: Final recap: 283 verified quotes from 171 voices; opposition outnumbers support about two to one. None of the 31 members of Congress on record supports the move; the WSJ editorial board called it "a political bailout." China's foreign ministry had no comment and Singapore's PM Wong said "So be it." Asia rallied Tuesday (TAIEX +9%), but NVDA gave back about 7% by 10:21 AM ET. Ives raised his target to $250.

label: Nov 24 end of day
note: NVDA closed Tuesday at $155.38, down 5.9%, and the chip index fell 7.9%; after hours it was $151.86. 357 verified quotes from 216 voices. None of the 36 members of Congress on record supports the reinstatement, now including Sanders, Rick Scott and Katie Britt. Trump said a pardon is "always an option"; the FT's Lex called the return "a triumph of money over morals."

label: Nov 25 midday
